findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:161 — P1 confidence 100: `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;` wrongly models a realm capability as selected-user state, so every normal first-factor login where `context.getUser()` is null skips `fillContextForm` and loses conditional passkey login.

goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true when `user != null`, meaning it enables fillContextForm when a user IS selected. Looking at the diff, the condition `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))` in the authenticate() method is called after the user selection logic. The original code had `if (context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())` which filled the form when user was NULL. The new logic with `user != null` is intentional - it fills the context form when a user is already selected (re-authentication scenario). For initial login without a user, the conditional UI autocomplete in the username field handles passkey discovery. The finding incorrectly claims this breaks discoverable-passkey login.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at line 161 returns true when `user != null`, but looking at how it's called in `authenticate()` at line 115, it's called with `context.getUser()` which CAN be null during initial login. However, the original code at lines 113-116 (before the change) also had the condition `if (context.getUser() == null)` wrapping the passkey setup, meaning passkeys were ONLY set up when user was null. The new code at line 115 calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` which requires user != null, but this is OUTSIDE the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block now. Looking at the diff more carefully, the passkey setup was moved from inside the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block to outside it, and the condition changed. The new logic sets up passkeys when user IS NOT null, which is the opposite of before. This appears intentional for the re-authentication fix. The finding claims passkey UI is lost for initial login, but the original code also didn't set up passkeys when user was already selected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding raises a valid concern about test coverage. The new `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` override in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` returns `false` to suppress showing authenticators during conditional passkey login. However, the tests only verify that the WebAuthn form element exists (`notNullValue()`), not whether the authenticator list is populated or empty. The test `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` and similar tests check `driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))` exists, but this doesn't distinguish between a form with authenticators shown vs suppressed. A passkey login succeeding doesn't prove the suppression behavior works correctly - it could succeed regardless of whether authenticators are displayed. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for the new behavior introduced by the diff.
